subject: The fitted-bedroom journey from measure to installation
hook: Do I need to empty the bedroom before you fit?
fb:
A question we get asked a lot as fitting day gets close: "Do I have to empty the whole bedroom?"

No. What we need is the wardrobe wall clear, a bit of working space in front of it, and an easy route in from the front door. Empty the old wardrobe, take down anything fixed to that wall, and we'll do the rest — including covering your floors.

If you're planning a fitted bedroom for the autumn, getting the order right now saves stress later. Got a question of your own? Drop it in the comments or send it through here:
https://superiofurniture.com/furniture-installation/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=plan-ahead-for-autumn&utm_content=day-350
gbp:
Do I need to empty the bedroom before my fitted wardrobes are installed?

Not entirely. For fitting day, clear the wall where the wardrobes are going and leave a working space in front of it. Empty any old wardrobe you are replacing, and take down shelves, pictures or curtain poles fixed to that wall. A clear route from the front door to the bedroom helps too.

Our own installation team protects floors before bringing anything in, and your furniture arrives already assembled from our Hanley workshop, so there is no flat-pack mess. We confirm exactly what needs moving when we measure, so there are no surprises on the day.

Planning a fitted bedroom? Find out more about how we install.
